editorial:
Imagine turning eighteen and suddenly meeting yourself from twenty years in the future. That is exactly what happens to Elliott after a wild mushroom trip. You get to see this funny, messy dynamic between a free-spirited teenager and her 39-year-old self, who is basically a walking warning sign. The vibe is very laid-back and feels like a typical summer break, but with a weird sci-fi twist. It captures that scary feeling of not knowing who you will become while keeping things light and funny. You will feel for Elliott as she tries to figure out if she should listen to her older self or just live her life her own way.

The acting is the best part here because the two versions of Elliott feel like the same person but with different life baggage. The pacing is smooth, though some parts feel a bit slow while they talk through their feelings. If you like coming-of-age stories that make you think about your own life, you will love this.
endingExplained: After spending time with her older self, Elliott realizes that trying to avoid every mistake just makes life boring. She decides to embrace the chaos of being young. The older Elliott eventually fades away, leaving the younger one with a new sense of peace. She stops obsessing over the future and chooses to focus on her family and friends in the present, knowing that growing up is a messy but necessary process.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves quirky stories about growing up and family drama.
